<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request! Make sure to follow the instructions to write release notes for your PR — it should only take a minute or two: https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing/#writing-good-release-notes. Try running yarn generate:release-notes *before* pushing your PR for an interactive experience. -->

## Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Why is it needed? Please give context on the "why?": why do we need this change? What problem is it solving for you?-->
The Payees table showed only names and rule counts, so you couldn't tell which duplicate payee to keep or which ones were stale without opening each one. Now there's:
- **Server:** a new query returns each payee's transaction count and last-used date. It reads the same data as the "Show unused payees" filter, so deleted transactions are left out and merged payees count toward their target.
- **UI:** new **Transactions** and **Last Used** columns. Payees with no transactions show `0` / `Never` in muted text, and `…` shows while loading.
- **Refresh:** the counts and the unused-payees list reload together after a merge, an undo or a sync. This also fixed two existing gaps: undo used to ignore transaction changes, and merges updated the unused list by guessing on the client instead of asking the server.
- **Tests, mutation testing reports and a release note.**
<!-- If AI tools wrote a significant part of this change, please disclose it here and name the tool you used. See https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing/ai-usage-policy -->
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
## Design

**Decision:** keep the unused-payees list and the new counts as two queries that read the same data, and always reload them together. This was the issue's main risk: the numbers had to agree with the unused filter and with merged payees.

**Alternatives:**
- **One combined server call:** guaranteed consistency, but it means changing the existing unused-payees code, which is a bigger and riskier change.
- **Work out "unused" from the counts on the client:** this would quietly change what "unused" means (e.g. payees referenced by rules), and that's out of scope.
- **Count from a different query:** this would duplicate the rules for deleted and merged rows, and risk the two disagreeing.

**Trade-off:** the two queries can briefly disagree while one has reloaded and the other hasn't.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- **Counting logic is in SQL.** It's faster, but mutation testing can't check it, so the server tests are its only protection.
- **Speed on large budgets wasn't measured,** and there's no database index for the payee lookup.
- **The two queries can briefly disagree** (the trade-off above).
- **Translations:** the rules column width fits English labels; a longer translation can misalign a row.
- **The refresh logic has no automated tests.**
- **Stryker configs and the merge script are course-only files.**

**Encountered:**
- **Stryker's Vitest runner doesn't work with this repo's Vitest version,** so I used my teammates' command-runner workaround.
- **Two existing gaps in the Payees page's refresh logic** (undo, merge) were fixed here because they affected the new columns.
- **Left alone:** older files that skip strict type-checking, some existing lint warnings, and the "1 associated rules" wording.



## Related issue(s)

Closes #149 

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: two new columns in the right place | Payees VRT screenshot (pending regeneration); manual check | E2E / manual | AC text |
| AC2: counts non-deleted transactions; merges count toward target | Server tests: counting, deleted transactions, merges, splits | Unit | AC text; agreed split rule |
| AC3: latest date in the user's format | Server latest/future-date tests; helper date-format tests | Unit | AC text; agreed future-date rule |
| AC4: `0` / `Never`, muted | Server "no transactions" test; helper "unused" test | Unit | AC text |
| AC5: unused payees show `0` / `Never` | Server test comparing stats with the unused list | Unit | AC text |
| AC6: transfer payees counted | Server transfer-payee test | Unit | AC text |
| AC7: right-aligned tabular numbers | Manual check; VRT once regenerated | Manual | AC text |
| AC8: merge updates without reload | Server merge test; manual check | Unit + manual | AC text |
| AC9: up to date after transaction changes | Server deleted-transaction test | Unit (data only) | AC text |
| AC10: undo restores counts | Manual check (merge undo) | Manual | AC text |
| AC11: placeholder while loading | Helper loading test | Unit | AC text; `…` matches the Tags page |
| AC12: unit tests; existing tests pass | 17 new tests; existing payee unit and e2e tests pass | Unit + E2E | AC text |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** the refresh logic after merge, undo and sync has no test harness in the repo, so merge and merge-undo were checked by hand. Undoing a transaction delete, coming back to the page after adding or deleting a transaction, and the page staying usable while counts load weren't checked at all. Layout and styling will be covered by the VRT screenshots once regenerated.

**AI-written tests:** all 17 new tests were written by Claude Code. Their expected values come from the acceptance criteria and the agreed decisions, not from the code's output. Breaking the SQL by hand made the split tests fail, and Stryker found one weak test, which was fixed.

----

Show transaction count and last-used date on the Payees page
open
=====
## Summary
Add two columns to the Manage Payees page: **Transactions** (how many transactions use the payee) and **Last Used** (the date of the payee's most recent transaction). Today the table only shows each payee's name and how many rules it has. That makes it hard to decide which duplicate to keep when merging, or which payees are stale enough to delete.

## User Story
As someone cleaning up my payee list, I want to see how many transactions each payee has and when it was last used so that I can decide which payees to merge, keep, or delete without opening each one.

## User Scenario
Jordan imports transactions from two banks and has ended up with near-duplicate payees: `AMAZON.COM`, `Amazon`, `Amzn Mktp US`. Jordan opens **More → Payees** and searches for "amaz". Today all three rows look the same, apart from their names and rule counts, so Jordan can't tell which one is the "real" payee to merge the others into.

With this feature, the rows show:

- `Amazon` — 312 transactions, last used Oct 30, 2026
- `AMAZON.COM` — 18 transactions, last used Mar 2, 2025
- `Amzn Mktp US` — 1 transaction, last used Jan 14, 2024

Jordan selects all three, merges them into `Amazon`, and that row now shows 331 transactions. Later, Jordan sorts through old payees, sees `Joe's Pizza` with 2 transactions last used in 2022, and deletes it confidently.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The Manage Payees table header has two new columns, **Transactions** and **Last Used**, placed between **Name** and the existing rules button.
2. **Transactions** shows the number of non-deleted transactions whose payee is this payee. Transactions that point at a payee merged into this one count toward this payee.
3. **Last Used** shows the date of the payee's most recent non-deleted transaction, formatted with the user's date format setting.
4. A payee with no transactions shows `0` and `Never`, in a muted style.
5. Every payee shown by the existing **Show N unused payees** filter displays `0` / `Never`. (The reverse is not required: a payee with no transactions but referenced by a rule is not "unused" today and stays out of that filter.)
6. Transfer payees (e.g. "Transfer: Checking") also show their count and last-used date.
7. Counts are right-aligned and use tabular numerals so the digits line up in a column.
8. After merging payees, the target payee's count and last-used date update to include the merged payees' transactions, without a page reload.
9. After deleting a transaction, or adding one with a payee, then returning to the Payees page, the numbers are up to date.
10. Undoing a merge or delete restores the previous counts and dates.
11. The Payees page loads and stays usable while counts are being calculated; the new cells show a placeholder until data is ready.
12. Unit tests cover the counting logic: zero transactions, multiple transactions, deleted transactions not counted, merged payees counted toward the target, and the latest date picked correctly. The existing Payees tests still pass.

## Out of Scope
- Sorting the table by transaction count or last-used date.
- Filtering by these values (e.g. "not used in the last year").
- Showing dollar totals per payee.
- Suggesting which payees to merge.
- Changing what the existing **Show unused payees** filter counts as "unused".
- The mobile app's payees screen.

## Open Questions
- **Split transactions:** if a split transaction's children have different payees, do we count the parent's payee, each child's payee, or both?
- **Future-dated transactions:** if a payee's most recent transaction is dated in the future (e.g. entered ahead of time), should **Last Used** show that future date or the latest date up to today?
- **Scheduled transactions:** should schedules that haven't been posted yet count toward the total? (Proposed: no; only real transactions count.)
- **Clickable count:** should clicking the count open a transaction list filtered to that payee, like the **View Transactions** button on the Tags page?
- **Date format:** show a full date (`Oct 30, 2026`) or a relative one (`3 days ago`)?

## Rough Scope
**Size:** Medium. Estimated at about 200–350 lines across 6–8 files, similar in size to #128 (custom reports subcategory fix). Should fit within one sprint for one person, including tests. Smaller than it sounds because Actual already runs a similar count-and-latest-date query for its "common payees" list.

**Main risk:** keeping the numbers consistent with the rest of the Payees page, especially for merged payees and the **Show unused payees** filter (criteria 2, 5 and 8), and refreshing correctly after merge, delete and undo.

## Source
- **How it was found:** a review of the codebase for small features that are missing but easy to add, using this team's earlier closed PRs as a guide for size.
- **Gap in the current code:** the Payees table has only a Name column and a rules button showing each payee's rule count (`PayeeRuleCountLabel.tsx`). Nothing on the page shows how many transactions a payee has or when it was last used.
- **Existing building blocks:**
  - The **Show N unused payees** filter in `ManagePayees.tsx` already finds payees with no transactions, so Actual already tracks this data. The page just doesn't show it per payee.
  - `getCommonPayees` in `loot-core/src/server/db/index.ts` already runs a count and most-recent-date query per payee, for the payee autocomplete. A full-history version of that query would cover this feature.
  - `ManagePayeesWithData.tsx` already refreshes rule counts after sync and undo, and the new columns can follow the same pattern.
- **Related work:** complements the Tags-page usage count issue and the earlier Payee Merge / Cleanup Tool issue (#6). It does not duplicate any open or closed issue in this repo.

diff --git a/packages/desktop-client/src/components/payees/payeeUsageDisplay.test.ts b/packages/desktop-client/src/components/payees/payeeUsageDisplay.test.ts

@@ -0,0 +1,81 @@
+import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
+
+import { getPayeeUsageDisplay } from './payeeUsageDisplay';
+
+const baseArgs = {
+  dateFormat: 'MM/dd/yyyy',
+  neverLabel: 'Never',
+};
+
+describe('getPayeeUsageDisplay', () => {
+  it('shows a placeholder in both cells while loading', () => {
+    // A literal, not the exported constant: comparing against the constant
+    // would still pass if it were emptied, leaving the cells blank
+    expect(
+      getPayeeUsageDisplay({ ...baseArgs, stats: undefined, isLoading: true }),
+    ).toEqual({
+      count: '…',
+      lastUsed: '…',
+      isLoading: true,
+      isUnused: false,
+    });
+  });
+
+  it('shows 0 and the never label, muted, for a payee with no transactions', () => {
+    expect(
+      getPayeeUsageDisplay({ ...baseArgs, stats: undefined, isLoading: false }),
+    ).toEqual({
+      count: '0',
+      lastUsed: 'Never',
+      isLoading: false,
+      isUnused: true,
+    });
+  });
+
+  it('uses the never label it is given, so it can be translated', () => {
+    const display = getPayeeUsageDisplay({
+      ...baseArgs,
+      neverLabel: 'Nunca',
+      stats: undefined,
+      isLoading: false,
+    });
+
+    expect(display.lastUsed).toBe('Nunca');
+  });
+
+  it('shows the count and last-used date for a used payee', () => {
+    expect(
+      getPayeeUsageDisplay({
+        ...baseArgs,
+        stats: { count: 312, lastUsed: '2026-10-30' },
+        isLoading: false,
+      }),
+    ).toEqual({
+      count: '312',
+      lastUsed: '10/30/2026',
+      isLoading: false,
+      isUnused: false,
+    });
+  });
+
+  it("formats the date with the user's date format", () => {
+    const stats = { count: 1, lastUsed: '2024-01-14' };
+
+    expect(
+      getPayeeUsageDisplay({
+        ...baseArgs,
+        dateFormat: 'dd.MM.yyyy',
+        stats,
+        isLoading: false,
+      }).lastUsed,
+    ).toBe('14.01.2024');
+    expect(
+      getPayeeUsageDisplay({
+        ...baseArgs,
+        dateFormat: 'yyyy-MM-dd',
+        stats,
+        isLoading: false,
+      }).lastUsed,
+    ).toBe('2024-01-14');
+  });
+});
diff --git a/packages/desktop-client/src/components/payees/payeeUsageDisplay.ts b/packages/desktop-client/src/components/payees/payeeUsageDisplay.ts
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..212862dc2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/desktop-client/src/components/payees/payeeUsageDisplay.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
+import type { PayeeUsageStats } from '@actual-app/core/server/payees/app';
+import * as monthUtils from '@actual-app/core/shared/months';
+import type { Locale } from 'date-fns';
+
+// Shown in both cells until the usage stats have loaded
+export const USAGE_LOADING_PLACEHOLDER = '…';
+
+export type PayeeUsageDisplay = {
+  count: string;
+  lastUsed: string;
+  isLoading: boolean;
+  // No transactions: shown as "0" / "Never" in a muted style
+  isUnused: boolean;
+};
+
+type GetPayeeUsageDisplayArgs = {
+  // Undefined when the payee has no transactions
+  stats: PayeeUsageStats | undefined;
+  isLoading: boolean;
+  dateFormat: string;
+  locale?: Locale;
+  // Translated by the caller, so this stays free of React and i18n
+  neverLabel: string;
+};
+
+export function getPayeeUsageDisplay({
+  stats,
+  isLoading,
+  dateFormat,
+  locale,
+  neverLabel,
+}: GetPayeeUsageDisplayArgs): PayeeUsageDisplay {
+  if (isLoading) {
+    return {
+      count: USAGE_LOADING_PLACEHOLDER,
+      lastUsed: USAGE_LOADING_PLACEHOLDER,
+      isLoading: true,
+      isUnused: false,
+    };
+  }
+
+  if (!stats) {
+    return {
+      count: '0',
+      lastUsed: neverLabel,
+      isLoading: false,
+      isUnused: true,
+    };
+  }
+
+  return {
+    count: String(stats.count),
+    lastUsed: monthUtils.format(stats.lastUsed, dateFormat, locale),
+    isLoading: false,
+    isUnused: false,
+  };
+}

+// Vitest config for mutation testing the Payees usage display (issue #149)
+// with StrykerJS. stryker.issue-149.config.json runs it once per mutant.
+//
+// Based on Bennett Matuszewski's vitest.stryker.config.mts from #163: a
+// standalone config rather than the full vite.config.mts, which copies
+// public assets every time it loads and fails when Stryker's parallel
+// workers load it at the same time. The helper's tests only need module
+// resolution: no JSX, no i18n, no DOM.
+import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
+
+export default defineConfig({
+  resolve: {
+    conditions: ['electron-renderer', 'module', 'browser', 'default'],
+    tsconfigPaths: true,
+  },
+  test: {
+    include: ['src/components/payees/payeeUsageDisplay.test.ts'],
+    environment: 'node',
+    globals: true,
+  },
+});

+// Reads the same view as `orphanedPayeesQuery`, so every orphaned payee is
+// absent here. The view already resolves merged payees to their target and
+// drops deleted transactions (and children of deleted parents). A split
+// counts once per distinct payee on it, whether on the parent or a child.
+export function getPayeeUsageStats() {
+  return all<{
+    payee: DbPayee['id'];
+    count: number;
+    last_date: DbViewTransactionInternalAlive['date'];
+  }>(`
+    SELECT payee,
+      COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(parent_id, id)) AS count,
+      MAX(date) AS last_date
+    FROM v_transactions_internal_alive
+    WHERE payee IS NOT NULL
+    GROUP BY payee
+  `);
+}

+// Payees without any transactions are omitted; callers treat a missing
+// entry as 0 transactions, never used.
+async function getPayeeUsageStats(): Promise<
+  Record<PayeeEntity['id'], PayeeUsageStats>
+> {

# Mutation testing: Issue #149 -- Transactions and Last Used columns on the Payees page

**PR(s):** (https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/189)  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.0.0 (command runner; see [Setup notes](#setup-notes))  **Config:** [`packages/loot-core/stryker.issue-149.config.json`](../../../packages/loot-core/stryker.issue-149.config.json) (server), [`packages/desktop-client/stryker.issue-149.config.json`](../../../packages/desktop-client/stryker.issue-149.config.json) and [`vitest.stryker.issue-149.config.mts`](../../../packages/desktop-client/vitest.stryker.issue-149.config.mts) (client), based on Bennett Matuszewski's setup from #163 and the #97 setup  **Command:** `cd packages/loot-core && npx stryker run stryker.issue-149.config.json`, then `cd packages/desktop-client && npx stryker run stryker.issue-149.config.json`, then `node docs/sprint3/mutation/scripts/merge-stryker-reports.mjs <out.json> packages/loot-core=<core report> packages/desktop-client=<client report>` from the repo root
**Reports:** [before](reports/149-icsasso-before.json) · [after](reports/149-icsasso-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 96.00% → after 100.00%

|        | Mutants | Killed | Timed out | Survived | Score   |
| ------ | ------- | ------ | --------- | -------- | ------- |
| Before | 25      | 24     | 0         | 1        | 96.00%  |
| After  | 25      | 25     | 0         | 0        | 100.00% |

| File                                     | Before          | After            |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------- |
| `loot-core/.../db/index.ts` (815–828)    | 100.00% (2/2)   | 100.00% (2/2)    |
| `loot-core/.../payees/app.ts` (41, 95–114) | 100.00% (4/4) | 100.00% (4/4)    |
| `desktop-client/.../payeeUsageDisplay.ts` | 94.74% (18/19) | 100.00% (19/19)  |

**What was mutated.** The source code the PR adds that has unit tests:

- `packages/loot-core/src/server/db/index.ts`, lines 815–828: `getPayeeUsageStats()`, the SQL query that counts each payee's transactions and finds the latest date.
- `packages/loot-core/src/server/payees/app.ts`, line 41 (registering the `payees-get-usage-stats` handler) and lines 95–114 (the handler, which turns the query rows into `{ count, lastUsed }` per payee).
- `packages/desktop-client/src/components/payees/payeeUsageDisplay.ts`, the whole file: `getPayeeUsageDisplay()`, which decides what the Transactions and Last Used cells show (loading placeholder, `0` / `Never`, or the count and formatted date).

The rest of `db/index.ts` (1,259 lines) and `app.ts` is unrelated to #149, so the configs mutate only these line ranges. The PR's React component changes (`PayeeTableRow.tsx`, `PayeeTable.tsx`, `ManagePayees.tsx`, `ManagePayeesWithData.tsx`) are left out: no unit test renders them, so every mutant there would survive as untested code. #97 left out its one-line component change for the same reason. I checked those changes by hand in the running app instead (see Q1).

The tests run are `packages/loot-core/src/server/payees/app.test.ts` (12 usage-stats tests plus the existing rule-count test) and `packages/desktop-client/src/components/payees/payeeUsageDisplay.test.ts` (5 tests).

## Setup notes

- **Command runner, as in #163 and #97.** The Vitest runner (`@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.0.0) runs no tests for any mutant with the repo's Vitest 5, so every mutant "survives" ([125-bennettmatuszewski.md](125-bennettmatuszewski.md) documents this). I used the same workaround: Stryker's command runner starts Vitest once per mutant (`--bail 1 --maxWorkers 1`). Every mutant in both reports has `testsCompleted: 1`, so none of the results comes from the broken runner.
- **Two packages, one report.** The PR's server code is in loot-core and its display helper is in desktop-client, which have separate Vitest setups, so there is one Stryker config per package. [`scripts/merge-stryker-reports.mjs`](scripts/merge-stryker-reports.mjs) merges the two JSON reports into one: it prefixes each file path with its package folder, makes mutant and test ids unique, and prints the score per file and in total with Stryker's formula. On the client report alone it gives the same 94.74% Stryker printed.
- **Line ranges.** The server config uses Stryker's `file:start-end` syntax. Without it, Stryker would mutate all of `db/index.ts`, and each server mutant takes about 75 seconds (mostly loot-core's test setup).
- **Server tests use loot-core's own config.** `ENV=node npx vitest --run src/server/payees/app.test.ts` uses loot-core's normal `vitest.config.ts`, which already excludes `.stryker-tmp`. The client uses a standalone `vitest.stryker.issue-149.config.mts` like #97's, because the full `vite.config.mts` fails when Stryker's workers load it at the same time.
- **Checked before running.** Both test commands passed on unchanged code before each Stryker run (13 server tests, 5 client tests).
- **No timeouts.** Both packages ran at `concurrency: 2`, one package after the other, so the machine was never running more than two test processes. No mutant timed out in either run.
- **Same mutants before and after.** The source files did not change between the runs; only the test did. I compared the two reports mutant by mutant: both have the same 25 mutants (same file, position, mutator and replacement), and the only status change is `payeeUsageDisplay.ts:6`, Survived → Killed.
- **Commits.** [`fd98273fe`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/commit/fd98273fe) is the code and tests the before run saw. [`88dff722a`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/commit/88dff722a) adds the configs, the merge script and the before report. [`aff6ef516`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/commit/aff6ef516) is the strengthened test, and [`cb42279ac`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/commit/cb42279ac) adds the after report.

## Surviving mutants

The before run had one survivor, in a line this PR added. "Gap" = a test was missing or too weak; "Equivalent" = no test can tell the mutant from the original.

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| payeeUsageDisplay.ts:6 | `USAGE_LOADING_PLACEHOLDER = '…'` → `""` | Gap | The loading test compared the result to the exported `USAGE_LOADING_PLACEHOLDER` constant instead of a literal. When the mutant empties the constant, the expected value is emptied too, so the test can't fail. The behavior does change: while the counts load, the Transactions and Last Used cells would be blank instead of showing `…`. AC11 asks for a placeholder until the data is ready, so the mutant is not equivalent. Killed by `payeeUsageDisplay.test.ts › getPayeeUsageDisplay › shows a placeholder in both cells while loading`, which now expects `'…'`. |

**Totals:** 1 survivor = 1 gap, killed. The after report has no survivors.

For context, the 24 mutants killed in the before run:

- **Server (6):** emptying `getPayeeUsageStats()` (db/index.ts:815), replacing the SQL with an empty string (820), renaming the handler to `""` (app.ts:41), and emptying the handler (104), its loop (107) or each `{ count, lastUsed }` entry (108). Every usage-stats test kills these.
- **Client (18):** flipping `if (isLoading)` and `if (!stats)`, emptying `'0'` and the returned objects, flipping each `isLoading` / `isUnused` flag, and so on. The tests compare the whole returned object with `toEqual`, so any changed field fails them.

## New or strengthened test

Commit: [`aff6ef516`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/commit/aff6ef516) · Test: `packages/desktop-client/src/components/payees/payeeUsageDisplay.test.ts › getPayeeUsageDisplay › shows a placeholder in both cells while loading` (strengthened: expects the literal `'…'` instead of the exported constant, with a comment saying why) · Kills: `payeeUsageDisplay.ts:6` (`'…'` → `""`), shown as Killed in the after report.

The source code was not changed for this; only the test's expected value.

## Questions

**1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**

The one survivor showed a test that couldn't fail: the loading test took its expected value from the code under test (the exported placeholder constant), so whatever the constant held, the test agreed with it. The fix was to write down the value the requirement asks for.

The 100% server score shows more about the tool than about the tests. The logic that matters for #149 is in the SQL: counting a split once per payee (`COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(parent_id, id))`), taking the latest date, and leaving out deleted and merged-away transactions through the `v_transactions_internal_alive` view. To Stryker the whole query is one string, so its only mutation there was emptying it, which any test kills. To check that the tests guard the SQL itself, I changed `COUNT(DISTINCT …)` to `COUNT(*)` and exactly the two split tests failed, then I restored the line. That manual check isn't part of the D6 score (since it wasn't with a tool), but it is why I trust the server tests more than the 6 server mutants alone would justify.

The mutation score also says nothing about the React wiring: refetching after a merge, an undo or a sync, and the columns lining up. No unit test renders those components, so I checked them in the running app with the demo budget: merging two payees updated the target's count and last-used date without a reload, and Ctrl+Z restored both payees' numbers.


**2. Did any survivor expose an assertion whose expected value wasn't based on the requirements?**

Yes. The loading test's expected value was `USAGE_LOADING_PLACEHOLDER`, the implementation's own constant, not something from the requirements. AC11 asks for a placeholder until the data is ready, and the `…` was chosen during implementation to match the Tags page's count column. The fixed test expects `'…'`.

The other expected values come from the acceptance criteria or from the open-question decisions made before implementation: a split counts once for each payee on it, and Last Used shows a future date if that is the latest transaction. For example, the split tests expect `count: 1` because of the agreed split rule, not because that is what the query happened to return.

**3. AI use, and what was verified or corrected.**
Claude Code drafted the implementation plan and suggested answers to the open questions; the decisions (split counting, future dates, no clickable count, refetching both lists together, keeping the counting in SQL) were made by me. Claude also wrote the Stryker configs (based on the #97 / #163 setup), the merge script, and ran both passes.
- What was checked rather than taken on trust: both test commands passed before each Stryker run; every mutant has `testsCompleted: 1` (not the broken-runner "survivors"); the merge script reproduces Stryker's own 94.74%; the before and after reports have the same 25 mutants, with only the one status change; the manual `COUNT(*)` check; the browser check of alignment, merge and undo.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 17:35:01Z)**_

**What it is:** knip looks for files, dependencies and binaries in the repo that nothing uses. It flags exactly one thing in this PR:

```
Unused files (1)
docs/sprint3/mutation/scripts/merge-stryker-reports.mjs
```

That's the course-only script that merges the two Stryker reports. You run it by hand with `node`, so nothing imports it. knip only treats a file as used if something imports it or [knip.json](knip.json) lists it as an entry point, and this one is neither. The PR did add `vitest.stryker.issue-149.config.mts` to knip.json, but not this script. It has nothing to do with the Payees feature. The app code passes knip.

**How necessary:** fix it before merging, but it's a minor problem.
- knip passes on master right now, and it runs as part of CI ([check.yml](.github/workflows/check.yml)). Merging as-is would make master's CI fail, and every later PR would show the same knip failure until someone fixed it. That would land on teammates, not just this PR.
- I couldn't tell whether the branch rules actually block merging on a failed knip check, because that needs GitHub access I don't have here. Even if they don't, leaving CI red on master is the real cost.
- It doesn't change how the app behaves at all.

**The fix** is one line. In the root workspace of [knip.json:13](knip.json#L13), mark the script as an entry point:

```json
"entry": ["bin/*.mts", "docs/**/scripts/*.mjs"],
```

I'd use `entry` instead of `ignore`: knip will then still check the script's own imports, and later mutation scripts in `docs/` will be covered too. Adding `"docs/**"` to the `ignore` list a line below would also work. I can make the change on the branch if you want.
